claims.value: Napoleon’s note gives side A 23,000 in Bessières’s territorial corps, 17,000 active and scarcely 15,000 for the projected Benavente affair.
claims.rationale: The note is dated on the battle day but projects a different location and includes troops moving or in garrisons. None is certified as the Medina battlefield total. English rendering (ours): "Bessières commands the Western Pyrenees corps, 23,000 infantry, cavalry and artillery; his active forces are 17,000, scarcely 15,000 for the Benavente affair."

claims.value: Toreno gives side B 15,000 in Blake’s marching force and 22,000 combatants with Cuesta, with fewer than 500 horsemen.
claims.rationale: Pre-engagement combined force, not all simultaneously engaged; preserves the cavalry alternative to Bodart. English rendering (ours): "This force was 15,000, making 22,000 combatants with Cuesta’s; many were peasants still in their ordinary clothes, and the horsemen did not reach 500."

claims.value: Toreno says the Castilian commander took chief command by seniority when the armies joined.
claims.rationale: This is Toreno’s characterization of seniority and troops, not a quality score. English rendering (ours): "Once both generals joined, the Castilian commander took command as the senior, although his troops were fewer and of inferior quality."

claims.value: Toreno places Cuesta behind, on the other side of the road from Blake, with a considerable gap.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "Cuesta stood behind on the other side of the road, leaving a considerable gap between his troops and Blake’s."
